title: Discussing problems
about: Phrasal verbs for talking about problems: how things go wrong (botch up, break down, run into difficulties, land in trouble) and how people deal with them (bear up, resign yourself to, iron out, fall back on, make up for, resort to).

items.pattern: sth hangs over sb · often continuous: be hanging over sb · not separable: it's hanging over me · subjects: an exam, a decision, a debt, a threat, a court case
items.meaning: something unpleasant that may happen keeps worrying you, because it hasn't been settled yet
items.uk: нависати над кимось, не давати спокою
items.example: The driving test has been **hanging over** me all week, so I'll be glad when it's done.
more: With a rent rise **hanging over** us, we've stopped eating out.
I hate having unpaid bills **hanging over** me, so I pay them the day they arrive.
items.watchOut: Не плутай із hangover — похмілля (іменник, одне слово). Тут дієслово: неприємна справа «висить» над тобою. Людина стоїть після over: it's hanging over me.

items.pattern: botch up sth · botch sth up · botch it up (not botch up it) · also with no object: botch up · informal
items.meaning: do something so badly that you spoil it or cause problems
items.example: The builders **botched up** the bathroom, and now water drips into the kitchen.
more: I tried to cut my own fringe and completely **botched it up**.
The airline **botched up** our booking, so we had no seats on the flight home.
items.watchOut: Розмовне слово: у листі до незнайомої людини краще made a mistake або handled it badly. Із займенником — botch it up, а не botch up it.

items.pattern: sth breaks down · no object · subjects: a marriage, a relationship, talks, negotiations, communication · noun: the breakdown of a marriage, a breakdown in communication
items.meaning: (a relationship or talks) fail and stop working
items.example: Their marriage **broke down** after years of arguing about money.
more: Talks between the landlord and the tenants **broke down**, so the case went to court.
Communication in our family **broke down** completely after Grandad's will was read.
items.watchOut: У break down кілька значень: зламатися (про машину), розплакатися (she broke down in tears), розпастися (про стосунки, переговори). Про пару, що розійшлася, частіше кажуть they broke up. Break out — спалахнути (про війну, пожежу), це інше.

items.pattern: sth spills over into sth · no object · subjects: stress, anger, a problem, a row, a crowd · past: spilled / spilt over
items.meaning: (a problem, feeling or crowd) spreads into another area or another part of life and affects it
items.example: She tries not to let stress from work **spill over** into her weekends.
more: The argument at the bar **spilled over** into the street.
When the kids fall out at school, it often **spills over** into home life.
items.watchOut: Після spill over зазвичай into: problems spill over into family life, а не spill over on (калька з «перекинутися на»). Про натовп чи рідину на поверхню — onto: the crowd spilled over onto the pitch. Буквально spill — пролити; тут образно, як рідина, що переливається через край.

items.pattern: get / be caught up in sth · object after in · objects: a crowd, a protest, traffic, a row, a scandal, the excitement
items.meaning: become involved in a situation, often without wanting to, so that it's hard to get out of it
items.uk: опинитися втягнутим у щось, застрягти в чомусь
items.example: We **got caught up in** the crowds after the match and missed the last train.
more: I don't want to **get caught up in** my sisters' argument again.
He **got caught up in** the excitement of the auction and paid far too much for a lamp.
items.watchOut: Прийменник — in: caught up in a row. Не плутай з catch up with sb — наздогнати когось, і з catch up on sth — надолужити (сон, новини).

items.pattern: run into problems / difficulties / trouble / debt / delays · not separable: run into them
items.meaning: start to have problems or difficulties
items.example: We **ran into** problems as soon as we tried to book a table for twelve.
more: If you **run into** any trouble with the boiler, give me a ring.
They **ran into** debt after buying a car they couldn't really afford.
items.watchOut: «Зіткнулися з проблемами» — ran into problems, а не collided with problems: collide — фізично зіткнутися. Run into sb — інше значення: випадково зустріти когось (I ran into Olena at the market).

items.pattern: land in hospital / prison / court / trouble / debt · sth lands sb in sth: it landed him in trouble · British: in hospital, in court, no article
items.meaning: end up in an unpleasant place or situation, often unexpectedly
items.example: He tried to fix the roof himself and **landed in** hospital with a broken leg.
more: Lying on your CV could **land** you **in** serious trouble.
She **landed in** debt after a year of shopping on credit cards.
items.watchOut: «Потрапити в лікарню» — land in hospital або end up in hospital. Прийменник — in, а не into, і в британській англійській без артикля: in hospital, in court.

items.pattern: no object · How are you bearing up? · bear up under sth (the strain, the pressure) · bear – bore – borne
items.meaning: stay strong and keep going in a sad or difficult situation
items.example: My mum's been **bearing up** really well since Dad went into the care home.
more: I know the move has been tough. How are you **bearing up**?
The kids **bore up** brilliantly on the twelve-hour journey.
items.watchOut: «Як ти тримаєшся?» — How are you bearing up? (або holding up), а не How are you holding yourself? — це про поставу. Минулий час — bore up.

items.pattern: be riddled with sth bad · passive form · objects: mistakes, holes, damp, woodworm, disease, corruption
items.meaning: be full of something bad or unpleasant
items.uk: рясніти чимось поганим, бути ураженим (хворобою, шашелем)
items.example: The old cottage was cheap because it **was riddled with** damp.
more: My first essay **was riddled with** spelling mistakes.
The plot of the film **is riddled with** holes, but I still enjoyed it.
items.watchOut: Прийменник — with: riddled with mistakes, не riddled of. Тільки про погане: про щось приємне кажуть full of. Riddle тут не «загадка».

items.pattern: resign yourself to sth / to doing sth · reflexive: myself, ourselves… · be resigned to sth · to + -ing, not to + infinitive
items.meaning: accept that something you don't want is going to happen, and stop fighting it
items.example: When the snow started, we **resigned ourselves to** spending the night at the airport.
more: I've **resigned myself to** the fact that I'll never be good at maths.
She seems **resigned to** losing the flat when the lease ends.
items.watchOut: «Змиритися з» — resign yourself TO, а не with. Після to — -ing: resign myself to waiting, а не to wait. Без yourself resign означає звільнитися з роботи.

items.pattern: safeguard against sth (theft, illness, fraud, loss) · safeguard sb/sth from/against sth: safeguard your savings · rather formal
items.meaning: do things that help protect you from something bad happening
items.uk: убезпечитися від чогось, захиститися від чогось
items.example: A good lock on your bike is the best way to **safeguard against** theft.
more: Washing your hands often helps **safeguard against** colds and flu.
Travel insurance **safeguards against** losing money on a cancelled holiday.
items.watchOut: Без додатка — safeguard against: safeguard against theft. Слово досить офіційне: у розмові частіше кажуть protect yourself from/against.

items.pattern: walk away (from sth) · no object, from + the situation: a problem, a relationship, a deal, a job
items.meaning: stop being involved in a difficult situation instead of dealing with it
items.uk: піти, відмовитися від чогось (не розв'язавши проблему)
items.example: You can't just **walk away** every time a friendship gets difficult.
more: They'd paid a deposit, but they **walked away** from the house when the survey found problems.
After ten years he **walked away** from the family business.
items.watchOut: Після walk away — from, а не of: walk away from the deal. Walk out (of sth) — демонстративно вийти (зі зборів, з кімнати); walk out on sb — кинути когось.

items.pattern: live with sth · not separable: live with it · objects: a problem, the noise, pain, a decision · I can live with that = I can accept it
items.meaning: accept an unpleasant situation and carry on with your life
items.uk: миритися з чимось, жити з цим
items.example: The neighbours' dog barks all day, but we've learnt to **live with** it.
more: The room is a bit small, but for that price I can **live with** it.
My knee still hurts sometimes. It's something I'll have to **live with**.
items.watchOut: Live with sb — жити разом із кимось. Live with sth — змиритися з чимось неприємним і жити далі. I can live with that — «мене це влаштовує», хоч і не ідеально.

items.pattern: iron out sth · iron sth out · iron it out (not iron out it) · objects: problems, difficulties, differences, details
items.meaning: deal with small problems or differences so that things work smoothly
items.example: We still have a few details to **iron out** before the wedding.
more: The new bus timetable had some problems at first, but they've **ironed them out** now.
My brother and I **ironed out** our differences over a long lunch.
items.watchOut: Буквально iron — прасувати; тут образно: розгладити «складки» в плані. Частка — out, не over і не away. Із займенником — iron them out.

items.pattern: fall back on sth (savings, experience, a skill, a plan) / sb (your parents) · not separable: fall back on it · noun: a fallback
items.meaning: use or turn to something or someone when other things have failed or there's no other choice
items.uk: вдатися до запасного варіанту, покластися на когось/щось
items.example: When the restaurant closed, she **fell back on** her teaching qualification.
more: It's good to have some savings to **fall back on** if you lose your job.
If the barbecue gets rained off, we can always **fall back on** pizza.
items.watchOut: Три слова: fall back ON. Fall back — відступити; fall on — накинутися на щось або припасти на дату (my birthday falls on a Sunday). Something to fall back on — запасний варіант, «подушка безпеки».

items.pattern: smooth things over · smooth over sth (an argument, a disagreement, an awkward moment) · smooth it over
items.meaning: make a disagreement or problem seem less serious, usually by talking to the people involved
items.example: Dad forgot Mum's birthday, but flowers and dinner out **smoothed things over**.
more: I'll talk to the neighbours and try to **smooth things over** after last night's party.
We **smoothed over** our disagreement about the holiday and booked Spain.
items.watchOut: «Згладити конфлікт» — smooth things over; частка over обов'язкова. Smooth down — пригладити (волосся, сукню), це про інше.

items.pattern: clear up sth · clear sth up · clear it up (not clear up it) · objects: a misunderstanding, confusion, a mystery, a question
items.meaning: explain something or deal with it so that there's no more confusion or disagreement
items.example: One phone call **cleared up** the confusion about who was picking up the kids.
more: There's been a mix-up with your booking, but we'll **clear it up** today.
Can I **clear something up**? I never said you were lazy.
items.watchOut: «З'ясувати» факт — find out; розв'язати непорозуміння — clear up. Інші значення clear up: прибрати (clear up the kitchen), розпогодитися (it's clearing up), минути (про висип, кашель).

items.pattern: make up for sth / for doing sth · not separable: make up for it · objects: a mistake, lost time, being late · more than make up for sth
items.meaning: do something good so that a bad thing seems less important or is balanced out
items.example: I was late for the film, so I bought the popcorn to **make up for** it.
more: We're going to the seaside every weekend this summer to **make up for** lost time.
The food was a bit cold, but the view more than **made up for** it.
items.watchOut: Прийменник — for, а не to. Не плутай: make up — вигадати або помиритися; make up with sb — помиритися з кимось; make it up to sb — загладити провину перед кимось; make up for sth — компенсувати щось.

items.pattern: resort to sth / to doing sth · objects: threats, bribery, lying, shouting · to + -ing, not infinitive · noun: as a last resort
items.meaning: do something you'd rather not do, because nothing else has worked
items.example: When the kids wouldn't eat their vegetables, I **resorted to** hiding them in the pasta sauce.
more: The shop **resorted to** cutting prices to get rid of the winter coats.
I hope we won't have to **resort to** calling the police about the noise.
items.watchOut: «Вдатися до» — resort TO + -ing: resorted to shouting, а не resorted to shout. A resort — курорт; as a last resort — у крайньому разі. Вимова із /z/.

items.pattern: grasp at sth · not separable: grasp at it · objects: a chance, an opportunity, an offer, any excuse · idiom: grasp / clutch at straws
items.meaning: eagerly take a chance or offer, often because you're unhappy with how things are now
items.example: Bored in the village, he **grasped at** his cousin's offer of a room in the city.
more: She was so tired of renting that she **grasped at** the first chance to buy a place of her own.
The doctors gave him little hope, but he **grasped at** every new treatment.
items.watchOut: «Хапатися за» — grasp AT. Без at grasp означає міцно схопити або зрозуміти (grasp an idea). «Хапатися за соломинку» — grasp (clutch) at straws.

warmup.q: How are you ___ after the move?
warmup.explain: «Як ти тримаєшся?» — How are you bearing up? (або holding up). Holding yourself — це про поставу.

warmup.uk: Ми змирилися з тим, що відпустки цього року не буде.
warmup.q: We've ___ the fact that there'll be no holiday this year.
warmup.explain: Змиритися з — resign yourself TO, а не with. Resign from — звільнитися (з роботи).

warmup.uk: Я пригощу тебе вечерею, щоб загладити провину за запізнення.
warmup.q: I'll buy you dinner to ___ being late.
warmup.explain: Make up FOR sth — компенсувати, загладити. Compensate теж потребує for: compensate for.
Зіткнутися з труднощами — run into problems. Collide — фізично зіткнутися (про машини).

warmup.uk: Таксі не було, тож ми вдалися до автостопу.
warmup.q: There were no taxis, so we ___ hitchhiking.
warmup.explain: Вдатися до — resort TO; далі іменник або -ing: resort to hitchhiking.
Be riddled with — бути повним чогось поганого (помилок, дірок, вологи).

warmup.uk: Добре мати заощадження, на які можна покластися, якщо щось піде не так.
warmup.q: It's good to have savings to ___ if things go wrong.
warmup.explain: Fall back on — вдатися до запасного варіанту. Rely потребує on: savings to rely on.
Clear up a misunderstanding — розв'язати непорозуміння. Find out — дізнатися (факт).

A.q: Their relationship ___ because they never had time for each other.
A.explain: Break down — розпастися (про стосунки, переговори). Break out — спалахнути (про війну, пожежу); break away — відокремитися, вирватися.

A.q: I've had the tax form ___ me for weeks. I really must fill it in.
A.explain: Неприємна справа hangs over you — «висить» над тобою й не дає спокою.

A.q: Climbing that wall without a rope could land you ___ hospital.
A.explain: Land (sb) in hospital / trouble / court — опинитися в лікарні, у халепі, у суді. Прийменник — in.

B.q: When things get hard at home, he tends to ___ instead of talking it through.
B.explain: Walk away from sth — піти від проблеми, не розв'язавши її. Walk over sb — зневажливо поводитися з кимось; walk through — пройти крізь.

B.q: I don't love the colour of the new kitchen, but I can ___ it.
B.explain: I can live with it — мене це влаштовує, змирюся. Live on — жити на (гроші, їжу); live by — жити за (правилами).

B.q: The new timetable had a few problems at first, but they've all been ___ out now.
B.explain: Iron out problems — владнати дрібні проблеми, буквально «випрасувати». Press і fold з out у такому значенні не вживаються.

a friend going through a break-up

example.title: Our dream cottage
example.uk:
Коли ми купували будиночок, то знали, що дах увесь у дірках. Чого ми не знали, так це того, що попередній власник ще й напартачив з електропроводкою. Ми зіткнулися з проблемами вже першого тижня.

Заощадження майже закінчилися, тож мені довелося знову взятися за свій старий підробіток у кав'ярні на вихідних. Дружина трималася набагато краще за мене. «Місяць ми й з холодним душем проживемо», — сказала вона.

Потроху ми владнали найгірше. Ми жодного разу не подумали все кинути. А тепер, коли я сиджу в саду у променях вечірнього сонця, мені здається, що це літо винагородило нас за все.
example.en:
When we bought the cottage, we knew the roof was [[riddled with|a9]] holes. What we didn't know was that the last owner had [[botched up|a2]] the wiring too. We [[ran into|a6]] problems in the very first week.

Our savings were nearly gone, so I had to [[fall back on|b6]] my old weekend job at the café. My wife [[bore up|a8]] much better than I did. "We can [[live with|b4]] cold showers for a month," she said.

Slowly we [[ironed out|b5]] the worst of it. We never once thought of [[walking away|b3]]. Now, sitting in the garden in the evening sun, I feel this summer has [[made up for|b9]] everything.
